extracted.intended_audience: SABEW members and business journalists (individual reporters, freelancers, student journalists, and news organizations) preparing submissions for the Best in Business Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and entry requirements for submitting journalism work to the Society for Advancing Business Editing and Writing (SABEW) Best in Business Awards (annual contest covering work published in a calendar year). Includes eligibility, byline rules, size categories, element limits, submission mechanics, fees, and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: This competition covers work published, broadcast and posted in the calendar year 2025. International submissions are encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only work with a publication/broadcast/post date in the calendar year 2025 is eligible. Encourage international entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: SABEW membership requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Best in Business competition is open to all SABEW members whose membership is current through June 1, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must verify membership status prior to submission by logging into the membership database. Membership must be active through the stated date to be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership verification during submission (new requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: When beginning a submission in Award Force, you will be prompted to enter the email address of an active member who is listed as a contributor. The awards program will automatically verify SABEW membership and if the contributor is not an active SABEW member, the entry will be ineligible for submission until the membership has been renewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before beginning a submission, confirm the contributor’s email and membership status; an ineligible (non-active) contributor will block the entry until renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student eligibility and free membership
rubrics_metrics.description: All students can enter, and non-member students will receive a free one-year student membership (a savings of $25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student entrants who are not SABEW members are granted a complimentary one-year student membership when entering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-byline membership requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For entries with more than one byline, one person must have a current SABEW membership with an expiration date of June 1, 2026, or later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple authors are listed, ensure at least one listed author has the required active membership through the cutoff date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline limits and staff-entry rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to five individuals may be named on an entry. They should be the strongest contributors to the work. Entries where more than five journalists made substantial contributions must be submitted as a staff entry and individuals will not be named on the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name only up to five principal contributors; if more than five people contributed substantially, submit as a staff entry (no individual names on award).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple entries per outlet and single-story category restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit on the number of entries per news outlet; however, any individual story may only be entered into one story type and one story topic category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A newsroom may submit many entries, but each specific story/package can be entered in only one story type category and one story topic category (e.g., cannot enter same story as both Investigative and Explanatory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Size categories (organization grouping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories are broken out by size, determined by the news organization’s total editorial staff. Small: 50 or less editorial staff. Medium: 51-150 editorial staff. Large: 151+ editorial staff. Freelancers will be grouped based on the size of the outlet that published their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the size category that matches your organization’s editorial staff count. Freelancers use the publisher's outlet size for grouping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership entries size determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If an entry is the product of a partnership of two or more organizations, enter into the size category corresponding to the combined staffs of the partner organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add staff counts across partnering organizations to determine the correct size category for the entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission period and deadline times
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions for the 2025 Best in Business Awards are open December 1, 2025, to February 2, 2026. Submissions close on Monday, February 2 at 5 p.m. ET. Deadlines: Early-bird — Thursday, January 8, 2026, at 5 p.m. ET; Competition deadline — Wednesday, January 28, 2026, at 5 p.m. ET; Late deadline — Monday, February 2, 2026, at 5 p.m. ET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit within the posted window and by the specific cutoff times for the applicable fee tier. Time zone is Eastern Time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission platform and acceptable formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must be submitted through the online platform. Basic requirements include a URL where the entry is live and a username and password if the entry is behind a paywall. A PDF of the entry will also be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a live URL whenever possible; if behind a paywall include access credentials; alternatively upload a PDF. All submissions must go through the specified online system (Award Force).

rubrics_metrics.name: Element limits and element types
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise noted, an entry shall consist of no more than three elements. Elements should all contain the same theme, though they don’t need to be directly related to each other. An element can be a text, audio or video, or an interactive. Accompanying photos and static graphics will not be counted as elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit submissions to three core elements that share a thematic connection; supplemental photos/static graphics do not count toward the element limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of corrections/retractions/editors’ notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must include any corrections, retractions, or editors’ notes related to accuracy or fairness that were published in connection to the submitted work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submitted work had post-publication corrections or editorial notes, include them with the entry so judges can assess accuracy/fairness context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing entries and post-submission changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries can be saved and edited until the deadline, but corrections cannot be made to entries after submitting. Please verify that all the information in your entry is correct before submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the platform’s save/edit features prior to final submission. Once submitted, you cannot change entry content—double-check details and attachments beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry fees, fee tiers, and discounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry fees are based on the date of your submission. Deadlines and fees: General Excellence — $130 / $150 / $200 (early/competition/late); Story Type, Story Topic categories and Best Range of Work — $79 / $99 / $150; Students — $20 (includes free one-year student membership). Freelance journalists receive a $15 discount per entry using the code Freelancer (not usable for student category entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the appropriate fee based on category and the submission date; apply freelancer code if eligible and not entering student categories. Fee amounts vary by deadline tier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and right of use
rubrics_metrics.description: No part of any entry will be returned. SABEW reserves the right to use any part or the whole of any entry for publicity, educational or promotional purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By entering, submitters accept that materials may be retained and used by SABEW for publicity/education/promotional use; do not expect returned materials.
